overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law: in-person meetings open to the public at a physical location need not offer public remote access even when a member joins remotely. The February 13 allegation was untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that a member participating remotely by Zoom at the March 27 and April 24 meetings required the public also be offered remote access.
allegations.key_passage: There is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that a public body provide the public with remote access if the meeting is instead held in-person at a location that is open and physically accessible to the public, even if a public body member participates remotely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the same remote-access violation at a February 13 meeting, which was filed more than 30 days after that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint was filed more than 30 days after the February 13 meeting; therefore, we do not review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by the complainant: the letter notes the Commission apparently did not review the complaint at a meeting within the required 14 business days. Treated as an observation only.
allegations.key_passage: It does not appear the Commission reviewed the Open Meeting Law complaint during a meeting.
